arguments.text: 8000 m, out-and-back 1250 m legs. Let the hard start settle by ~3 min, then hold near pod sustainable power (cp_shaft ~162 W, check calibration against legs). Keep pod reserve above ~30% until 2000 m left, then spend it; finish cue at ~600 m left. Watch for incidents (rudder weed, radio course change, drift). Compare same-direction legs to separate current from fatigue.

arguments.text: 2.8 min, leg 1 (north): start settled, pod 173 W vs sustainable 168 W, pod reserve 75%. Boat-model reserve lower (62%) since boat power 123 W vs CP 102: push_local 0.22 > fitted push_along 0.13, so current helps more than fitted on north legs; boat-derived numbers likely too pessimistic here. Use pod reserve for pacing unless pod looks drifted.

arguments.text: You are right on pace, reserve is good. Long strokes, breathe.

arguments.text: 7.8 min: paddler said cooked, cannot hold; asked: 7/10 really hurting. Pod 171 W (CP 162), pod reserve 60%, fade 0. Boat-model reserve 15% (boat 115-119 W vs boat CP 102). Legs: out 3.24 m/s @174 W, back 2.95 @171 W, current ~0.14 fits; race boat/pod ratio 0.68 vs test 0.63. Either boat CP too low (likely; then true boat CP ~110 W) or pod reads ~8% low (then truly near empty). Reassured. Test: if boat reserve hits 0 by ~10 min and paddler does not collapse, set boat cp_w ~110.

arguments.reason: test hypothesis: boat reserve empty vs paddler not collapsing

text: reassure cue: pod shows 171 W near CP with 60% reserve, no fade, 7/10; paddler likely misjudging; collapse watch set

arguments.text: 9.5 min POD FAULT: pod fell 172 -> 140 W in ~1.5 min while stroke rate (63), speed through water (3.08) and boat-model power (115-117 W) stayed flat. Paddler did not slow: pod is drifting low. Distrust pod power, pod reserve (will refill falsely), push_local and sustainable_shaft_power from now. Pace from boat-model power/speed (current fit ~0.13 still good). Boat reserve just hit ~0 at 116 W vs boat CP 102: if no fade by ~12 min, boat CP is too low (try ~110).

arguments.text: Something on the rudder. One back-stroke to clear it, then go.

11.9 min: GPS speed stepped down ~0.06 m/s at race ~645 s (2.95 -> 2.88) with stroke rate 63 and pod flat ~133 W (pod still offset low since 9.5 min). Paddler 7/10, says boat feels heavy, something dragging. Read as weed/drag, not a blow-up. Cued clear_rudder at 11.9 min. Check: speed back to ~2.95 on south leg (3.24 north) means cleared.

no cue: slowdown alert reflects the back-stroke dip (41%) in the 30-s mean; recovery check already scheduled at ~13.3 min

arguments.reason: Boat test values (102 W / 9.5 kJ) say reserve empty since 10 min, yet paddler held 115-117 W boat power from 3 to 13 min with no fade. Before the pod drifted, pod and boat agreed at a ratio of 0.68 (pod CP 162 W x 0.68 = 110 W, pod reserve 20 kJ x 0.68 = 13.6 kJ). Pod now reads low (fault at 9.5 min), so the boat model must carry pacing.

arguments.text: 8000 m, out-and-back 1250 m legs. POD FAULT since 9.5 min (reads ~22% low): ignore pod power/reserve/push_local. Pace off boat-model power and reserve (boat CP corrected to 110 W, 13 kJ at 13.3 min). Hold near boat sustainable power; spend the rest from ~2000 m left; finish cue at ~600 m left. Weed cleared at 12 min (speed fell 0.06 m/s at steady rate; clear_rudder restored it): repeat if speed steps down again at steady rate and paddler reports drag. Paddler tends to say they are cooked: check fade before easing.

text: no cue: rudder cleared (speed back to 3.09, no fade); corrected boat CP to 110 W / 13 kJ so the boat model can replace the faulty pod

arguments.text: Hurting is normal here. Pace is right, it lasts. Stay smooth.

15.9 min: paddler again says cannot keep this up; 8/10 really hurting (7/10 at 8 min). Boat model: 113 W vs CP 110, reserve 57%, lasts past finish, fade -1.4%. Reassured again. If fade drops below -4% outside a turn or weed, consider a small ease.
